provider: Zenodo anonymous download throughput (the fetch-serving question)

egress.terms: Free and unmetered, and HTTP Range (206) is supported anonymously, which is what makes the parallel read possible: 'accept-ranges: bytes', 'content-range: bytes 0-1023/81165133690'.

tooling: zenodo_get (pip) already parallelises; any HTTP client with range support (aria2c -x/-s, rclone non-backend http, curl --parallel) will do.
chaining: Per-connection shaping ~350-480 KB/s means you need concurrency, not accounts. Measured scaling: 1 conn 0.3 MB/s -> 6 conns 2.33 MB/s -> 16 conns 6.01 MB/s -> 32 conns 11.95 MB/s -> 64 conns 23.07 MB/s. Essentially linear, no knee up to 64.

limits.value: 50 GB per record default; 200 GB absolute ceiling on a single record with the 150 GB allowance pooled in; max 100 files per record (new API: 'a limit of 50GB total in the record (and any given file), and up to 100 files in the record').

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: Single-stream downloads are painfully slow (~215 KB/s on a 100MB range; the same range took 120s to deliver 45MB). Anything that does not parallelise will appear broken. Reading one file sequentially is a ~50x underuse of the link.
confidence_note: The read path and the served byte count were measured against the record's own object. The quota is still a page claim, so the record is documented and carries the probe. Was documented; now documented.

extras.verify_notes: All quota numbers confirmed unchanged. 1 conn 0.48 MB/s -> 8 conns 4.93 MB/s (10.3x for 8x) -> 32 conns 19.68 MB/s (4.0x for 4x, perfectly linear). The new-API file cap: 100 files per record, which matters for sharding — 50 GB must be split into no more than 100 files, i.e. >=500 MB per file.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
